newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 - Our final estimate on crude palm oil (CPO) production in October remains unchanged at 880,000 tonnes. This represents an increase of 1.8 percent over September and a growth of 14.5 percent over the same month last year. The modest month-on-month seasonal increase was contributed entirely by an additional working day in October. The performance of major producers/millers in Peninsular Malaysia mostly ranged from down 10 percent to up 10 percent. One producer did exceptionally well when its crop peaked with a 20 percent increase.

For the first 10 months this year, production is estimated at 6.98 million tonnes. This is 565,000 tonnes or 8.8 percent more than the corresponding period of 1995. Production for the whole of this year now looks likely to reach 8.41 million tonnes as against 7.81 million tonnes in 1995. The estimate on end-October stocks of palm oil also remains unchanged at 965,000 tonnes or some 70,000 tonnes more than month earlier. This comprises 605,000 tonnes CPO, up 80,000 tonnes, and 360,000 tonnes processed palm oil. Output of palm kernel/palm kernel oil also continued to exceed offtake.

This resulted in a further build-up in stocks of some 18,000 tonnes to an estimated 185,000 tonnes, oil basis. This is equivalent to about two months offtake in October. Palm oil exports by destinations figures for the first seven months this year published by PORLA show Pakistan has emerged as the largest market for Malaysian palm oil when its offtake rose strongly by 93,500 tonnes to 688,800 tonnes. China slipped into second place when it cut its offtake drastically by 198,600 tonnes to 617,700 tonnes.

However, the star performer remained India when it raised its shipments substantially by 149,200 tonnes or 45.8 percent to 475,200 tonnes. The combined offtake by Pakistan and India, at 1.164 million tonnes in January-July, represents 30.2 percent of Malaysian palm oil exports, an improvement over the 27.7 percent market share in 1995. The increased offtake of 242,700 tonnes by India and Pakistan also exceed the growth in exports of 164,900 tonnes to 3.856 million tonnes recorded by Malaysia in January-July.

In the 10 months to October, Malaysian palm oil exports expanded 465,000 tonnes to an estimated 5.93 million tonnes. Exports were at a robust level during August-October reflecting major contributions by various other destinations other than the Indian sub-continent, e.g. the European Union. Although exports are expected to contract seasonally from November onward in line with the increased output of oils from freshly harvested oilseed crops in major importing countries like India and Pakistan, they are projected to remain comfortably higher than year ago levels.

CPO futures meanwhile rose 25-29 ringgit in the last two days on chart-based buying by commission houses. However, cash values continued to lag in line with the sluggish product market. Prospect for the second largest ever U.S. soybean harvest this year at 2.403 billion bushels will not stimulate keen buying interest by consumers, particularly in the next several weeks.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
